title: The Prayers of Jesus
description: Walk with Jesus to the places where he prayed: before dawn in a solitary place, all night on a mountain, on the hillside where he taught the Lord's Prayer, at the tomb of Lazarus, beside Peter, in the garden of Gethsemane, on the cross, and at the last supper, where he prayed for you. Then pray with us, slowly, to close the day.

beats.say: He fed thousands, calmed storms, and raised the dead. But the one thing his disciples asked him to teach them was how to pray.
As he was praying in a certain place, when he ceased, one of his disciples said unto him: Lord, teach us to pray.
In this hour we will walk with Jesus to the places where he prayed, and we will pray his prayers with him, one at a time.
So find a quiet place, and breathe slowly. You do not need the right words tonight. You only need to come.
In Capernaum the day had been long. At evening the whole city was gathered together at the door, and he healed many that were sick.
And in the morning, rising up a great while before day, he went out, and departed into a solitary place, and there prayed.
Before anyone needed him, he went to his Father. And Luke tells us it was his habit: he withdrew himself into the wilderness, and prayed.
Simon and the others followed after him, and when they had found him, they said unto him: All men seek for thee.
He was ready for them. Prayer was not his escape from the work. It was where his strength for the work came from.
So tomorrow morning, before your phone, and before the noise of the day, give him the first quiet moment. He will meet you there.
There was a choice to be made: the twelve men who would carry his message to the world. He did not make it alone.
And it came to pass in those days, that he went out into a mountain to pray, and continued all night in prayer to God.
Hour after hour, under the stars, the Son of God talked with his Father about the people he loved.
And when it was day, he called unto him his disciples: and of them he chose twelve. Even Judas, he chose after a night of prayer.
If he prayed before his great decisions, how much more should we. Bring him the choice in front of you, and wait for his peace before you move.
On a hillside in Galilee, Jesus taught: But thou, when thou prayest, enter into thy closet, and pray to thy Father which is in secret.
For your Father knoweth what things ye have need of, before ye ask him. After this manner therefore pray ye:
Our Father which art in heaven, Hallowed be thy name. Thy kingdom come. Thy will be done in earth, as it is in heaven.
Give us this day our daily bread.
And forgive us our debts, as we forgive our debtors.
And lead us not into temptation, but deliver us from evil:
For thine is the kingdom, and the power, and the glory, for ever. Amen.
Pray it slowly tonight, one line at a time. Every line is a door: to his name, his will, his bread, his mercy, and his protection.
Five thousand men, and only five loaves and two fishes. And he looked up to heaven, and blessed, and brake the loaves.
Another day, he rejoiced in spirit, and said: I thank thee, O Father, Lord of heaven and earth, that thou hast hid these things from the wise and prudent, and hast revealed them unto babes.
At the tomb of his friend Lazarus, before anything had changed, Jesus lifted up his eyes, and said: Father, I thank thee that thou hast heard me.
And I knew that thou hearest me always. Then he cried with a loud voice: Lazarus, come forth.
He gave thanks before the miracle, not only after it. Thanksgiving is how faith speaks while it is still waiting.
Tonight, name three things, and thank him for each one. Then thank him for the answer you have not seen yet.
On his last night, Jesus looked at Peter, the boldest of them all, and saw what was coming before Peter could.
Simon, Simon, behold, Satan hath desired to have you, that he may sift you as wheat: But I have prayed for thee, that thy faith fail not.
That same night, by a fire in the high priest's courtyard, Peter denied him three times. And the Lord turned, and looked upon Peter.
His faith shook, but it did not fail, because someone had prayed. Days later, by the sea, Peter said: Lord, thou knowest all things; thou knowest that I love thee.
And when thou art converted, strengthen thy brethren. Whoever is failing near you tonight, you can do for them what he did for Peter. Pray for them by name.
Then were there brought unto him little children, that he should put his hands on them, and pray: and the disciples rebuked them. A teacher this important had no time for children, they thought.
But when Jesus saw it, he was much displeased, and said unto them: Suffer the little children to come unto me, and forbid them not: for of such is the kingdom of God.
And he took them up in his arms, put his hands upon them, and blessed them. Bring him the children you love tonight, by name. He has never once been too busy for them.
On the night he was betrayed, Jesus led his friends into a garden called Gethsemane. My soul is exceeding sorrowful, even unto death: tarry ye here, and watch with me.
And he went a little farther, and fell on his face, and prayed: O my Father, if it be possible, let this cup pass from me.
Nevertheless not as I will, but as thou wilt.
And there appeared an angel unto him from heaven, strengthening him. And being in an agony he prayed more earnestly.
He came back and found them asleep. Watch and pray, that ye enter not into temptation: the spirit indeed is willing, but the flesh is weak.
Then a second time: O my Father, if this cup may not pass away from me, except I drink it, thy will be done.
He told the Father exactly what he wanted, and then he trusted him with the answer. You are allowed to pray both: here is what I want, and thy will be done.
Mark kept the very word Jesus used in the garden, in his own language: Abba, Father, all things are possible unto thee; take away this cup from me: nevertheless not what I will, but what thou wilt.
Abba was the word a child used at home. Not a title for a distant king, but the first word a little one learns for the father who holds him.
And Paul wrote that we have received the Spirit of adoption, whereby we cry, Abba, Father. His word for God became ours. You may pray to God the way a child runs to a father.
On a hill outside Jerusalem, they nailed him to a cross between two thieves. And the first thing he said was a prayer.
Father, forgive them; for they know not what they do.
He prayed for the very men who were killing him. Whatever has been done to you, and whatever you have done, his prayer reaches further.
In the darkness he cried: My God, my God, why hast thou forsaken me? He was praying the words of a psalm. Even his prayers could be honest about the dark.
And at the last, crying with a loud voice: Father, into thy hands I commend my spirit. It is finished.
He ended his life the way he had lived it, in conversation with his Father. Into thy hands is a prayer for every night, and for the last one too.
At the end of the last supper, Jesus lifted up his eyes to heaven, and said: Father, the hour is come; glorify thy Son, that thy Son also may glorify thee.
I pray not that thou shouldest take them out of the world, but that thou shouldest keep them from the evil.
Then his prayer reached past that room, past that night, past two thousand years: Neither pray I for these alone, but for them also which shall believe on me through their word.
That they all may be one. If you believe, he was praying for you that night, long before you were born.
And he has not stopped. The scripture says he ever liveth to make intercession for them. Someone is praying for you right now.
Let us pray together now. Be careful for nothing; but in every thing by prayer and supplication with thanksgiving let your requests be made known unto God.
Lord Jesus, you rose before dawn to be with the Father. Teach me to come to you first, and to come to you often.
Our Father, hallowed be your name. Let your will be done in my home, in my work, and in my heart.
Forgive me, as I forgive those who have hurt me. I name them before you now, and I let them go.
Thank you for every answer I have seen, and for every one I have not seen yet. Pray for me, Lord, as you prayed for Peter, that my faith fail not.
Not my will, but yours be done. Into your hands I place my worries, my people, and my tomorrow.
And the peace of God, which passeth all understanding, shall keep your hearts and minds through Christ Jesus. Amen.
